title: The Gingerbread Boy's Emotions

description:
I think the Gingerbread Boy is a perfect way for children to lean and to express emotions. In the famous Gingerbread man story The Ginger Bread man story can be a great example for Social-emotional learning (SEL). SEL is the process of developing the self-awareness, self-control, and interpersonal skills that are vital for school, work, and life success.
Children with strong social-emotional skills are better able to cope with everyday challenges and benefit academically, professionally, and socially. From effective problem-solving to self-discipline, impulse control to emotion management and more, SEL provides a foundation for positive, long-term effects on kids, adults, and communities.
Children thrive. Schools win. Workplaces benefit. Society strengthens. All due to social-emotional learning.

description:

What is the purpose of the 4 seasons?
Season
Seasons have an enormous influence on vegetation and plant growth. Winter typically has cold weather, little daylight, and limited plant growth. Teaching children simple subtraction is very important because it builds the foundation for math skills they will need throughout school and life. Here are some key reasons:

Understanding “taking away” – Subtraction helps children understand what happens when something is removed, which is a concept they encounter daily (e.g., “I had 5 pumpkins  I took 2, now I have 3”).

Develops problem-solving skills – Learning subtraction strengthens logical thinking and teaches kids to approach problems step by step.

Prepares for higher math – Subtraction is one of the four basic operations in math. A solid understanding in kindergarten prepares children for addition/subtraction fluency, multiplication, division, and word problems later.

Builds number sense – Children learn how numbers relate to each other (for example, knowing that 6 – 2 = 4 also means 4 + 2 = 6). This improves flexibility with numbers.

Connects to real life – Kids use subtraction naturally: sharing snacks, counting toys, or noticing when something is missing. Teaching it early makes math feel practical and relevant.

Boosts confidence – Mastering subtraction at a young age helps children feel capable and confident in math, which encourages a positive attitude toward learning.
